entries.title: CLI update: freebuff-session-api

ai.title: Send client version header and add shared experiment bucketing
ai.summary: The CLI now attaches its version number to Freebuff session requests via the new `FREEBUFF_CLIENT_VERSION_HEADER`, allowing server-side friction logs to correlate refusals with the specific client build that encountered them. This observe-only header is read from `CODEBUFF_CLI_VERSION` and does not alter session behavior. The commit also introduces `common/src/util/stable-bucket.ts` for deterministic user bucketing in Postgres-backed experiments, using FNV-1a hashing with a lowbias32 finalizer to ensure uniform distribution across users with shared ID prefixes. Additionally, `common/src/util/stats.ts` provides dependency-free statistical helpers including Wilson intervals, Newcombe's difference test, and chi-square sample-ratio-mismatch checks for experiment readouts. Two other changes are included in this snapshot: the addition of shared constants and the introduction of new utility modules with their respective test suites.
ai.evidence: In `cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-api.ts`, the function `requestFreebuffSession` now reads `CODEBUFF_CLI_VERSION` and conditionally sets the `FREEBUFF_CLIENT_VERSION_HEADER` (defined in `common/src/constants/freebuff-desktop-sessions.ts` as 'x-freebuff-client-version') on outgoing session calls. The diff also adds `common/src/util/stable-bucket.ts` containing `experimentBucket`, `armForBucket`, and `validateArmWeights`, and `common/src/util/stats.ts` containing `wilsonInterval`, `newcombeDifference`, and `sampleRatioMismatch`.

ai.title: Mirror ten Desktop placements into Web chat inventory
ai.summary: A new module in `common/src/ads/web-desktop-placements.ts` maps ten Desktop ad slots (inline, breaks, partner, and billboard) to Web-only variants ending in the `:web` suffix. The shared placement registry in `common/src/constants/freebuff-placements.ts` now computes `PLACEMENT_SLOTS` by appending these web aliases to the original Desktop and mobile slots, giving them the `freebuff_web_chat` surface. The billboard module resolves web aliases back to their Desktop source so artwork requirements and shape checks apply identically to both variants. Campaign targeting logic treats a web alias as a target only if its Desktop source is explicitly targeted, preventing arbitrary suffixes from expanding campaign reach.

ai.title: Sponsored procedure bfcid placeholder resolution
ai.summary: Sponsored procedure templates now resolve `{bfcid}` placeholders directly within the execution prompt using the signed conversion token from `advertiserLink`. This change is gated by `resolveSponsoredBfcidTemplate`, which matches both literal and URL-encoded braces and returns null if the link is missing or invalid, triggering a new "unavailable" instruction in the prompt that forbids the model from inventing tokens or removing tracking parameters.

eli5.text: When an advertiser funds a task that runs unattended in the terminal, the assistant now automatically fills in a specific tracking code inside the task instructions using a secure token provided by the advertiser. If that token is missing or invalid, the assistant is instructed to skip any steps that require tracking and clearly state that attribution is unavailable, rather than guessing a value or removing the tracking requirement. This ensures that advertisers can accurately measure their campaign results without the user needing to manually configure anything, and the change has no direct effect on how you use the assistant for your own coding sessions.

ai.title: Add incremental gzip SSE decode tests for SDK
ai.summary: A new test suite was added to the `sdk` package to verify that the AI SDK client stack handles gzip-compressed Server-Sent Events incrementally rather than buffering the entire response. The tests use a local HTTP server to emit real gzip bytes with `Z_SYNC_FLUSH` intervals, mimicking the server-side behavior in `web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/sse-compression.ts`. This change ensures that text deltas from the `OpenAICompatibleChatLanguageModel` provider arrive spread out over time, preventing client-side buffering that would delay UI updates until the stream closes.
ai.evidence: New test file `sdk/src/impl/__tests__/sse-gzip-incremental-decode.test.ts` verifies that `OpenAICompatibleChatLanguageModel` from `@codebuff/llm-providers/openai-compatible` decodes `Content-Encoding: gzip` SSE responses incrementally using `Z_SYNC_FLUSH`, tracking delta arrival times to ensure they are spread out over time.
